thread:
catalina: Heads up — noticed a regression in canary today. Mid-length requests (~128-512 tokens) hitting prefill show ~15% p95 latency increase after the kernel-autotune v2.3 rollout. Chart: tinyurl.com/ri-canary-prefill :eyes:

sam: ugh, that matches the alerts I saw. p50 stable, p95/99 moved. Do we have kernel_name telemetry for those traces?

catalina: yes, I pulled a sample. Most of the affected traces got routed to kernel:fused-longctx-compute instead of fused-midseq-opt. route_reason tags often say "auto-autotune-winner".

sam: can you paste the log snippet?

catalina: sure — from a single affected request (anonymized):

```
[2026-03-18T10:11:03Z] req=abcd seq_len=256 route=path_prefill compute_kernel=fused-longctx-compute kernel_ms=42.7 kv_warm_ms=6.2 decode_ms=8.1
[2026-03-18T10:11:03Z] req=abcd baseline_expected_kernel=fused-midseq-opt baseline_expected_ms=32.8 decision=autotune_v2.3
```

sam: so kernel pick adds ~10ms. Is that consistent across HW? Ampere A100 or Graviton-ish?

catalina: most canary nodes are Ampere N2-family GPUs (Ampere Altra + pcie8?) — but we also saw similar on A100 canaries. GPU-specific perf delta seems larger on Ampere nodes.

ryan: I pulled a flamegraph and kernel-level profiler. Short summary: fused-longctx-compute has a fallback path that triggers extra shared-mem memcpy for mid-seqlen because of alignment assumptions; that memcpy scales poorly for the typical batch shapes we get at mid-slen. Flamegraph: tinyurl.com/ri-flame-midseq.

maria: that rings a bell — autotune v2.3 expanded the search space and favors kernels with better asymptotic perf at long ctx, but we didn't add hysteresis for mid-range where micro-ops cost wins. We should add a safety margin in the decision function to prefer kernels that win within a small epsilon for the observed distribution.

sam: Agreed. Short-term mitigation options: 1) force-route mid-slen [128..512] to fused-midseq-opt on canary; 2) roll back autotune v2.3; 3) tweak autotune scoring to add bias toward lower median latencies. Which do we do right now?

catalina: I prefer 1) for minimal blast radius. We can push a route override flag to canary only.

deploy-bot: canary-config-updater applied override: kernel_route_override=[128:512]=fused-midseq-opt to cluster=canary-west-1 at 2026-03-18T10:32:11Z :white_check_mark:

sam: after override, p95 dropped back ~12% in the canary within two deploy cycles. Good sign. But we need a proper fix in autotune scoring.

ryan: For the autotuner change I propose: add a penalty term P(seq_len, batch_shape, hw) that increases for kernels that incur extra memcopies for non-aligned sizes. Also cap the autotune window so it doesn't flip picks on small telemetry shifts. Pseudocode: 

```
score = median_latency + alpha * latency_std + beta * penalty(memcopy_victimness)
if abs(score - best_score) < hysteresis_epsilon: keep_current_pick
```

maria: Also add explicit KV-coldstart gating: many of the affected traces show kv_warm_ms spikes — prefills that come from a cold KV cache end up going to longctx path because the classifier uses historical avg but sees larger prefill time and flips. We should annotate route_reason with kv_state and run a targeted microbench where kv_cache_hit_rate=0.

catalina: Good call. Add telemetry keys: route.reason, kernel.name, seq_len_bucket, kv.cache_state, batch_shape, hw.family. We'll need to update the tracing schema and pipeline.

sam: I'll open two PRs: one to add the penalty/hysteresis to autotune core, and one to the routing config that supports per-cluster overrides and kv gating. I'll tag you both for review.

maria: For tests, let's add a microbenchmark that replays real mid-slen traffic shapes with kv cold and warm states and asserts kernel choice + p95 latency delta < 5%. Also add an autotune-self-check that compares new pick vs baseline on synthetic suite before promoting.

ryan: Logging reminder: route_reason strings need to include which autotune version made the call. e.g., "autotune_v2.3:score=xx:penalty=yy" — helps debugging.

catalina: Action items then:
- sam: PRs for autotune penalty + routing override support (ETA today EOD)
- ryan: microbench harness + flamegraph snippets (ETA tomorrow morning)
- maria: tracing schema update + kv cold/gate tests (ETA tomorrow midday)
- infra: keep the canary override until autotune patch lands and validated

sam: I'll also add a canary alert that fires if kernel choice flips >5% for any seq_len_bucket in 15m window — early detection for next rollouts.

maria: One more note — we should document the kernel capabilities table per hw in the model catalog. Autotune needs that metadata anyway. Adds transparency for SREs.

catalina: Thanks team. I'll follow up with a short postmortem once we close the autotune PR. For now the canary override is holding. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: canary override will remain in effect until 2026-03-19T00:00:00Z unless a config change is applied earlier.

sam: If anyone sees residual spikes, ping #eng-oncall and drop the sample ids here.

ryan: noted, I'll paste microbench results once ready.

maria: thanks all.
